blocks.text: The three states are to be enlivened by their primary source, the fourth.
blocks.directed: The three states are to be enlivened by their primary source, the fourth.

blocks.text: You Can Recognise Bhairava While Listening to Music. Finally, Some Good News.
blocks.directed: You Can Recognise Bhairava While Listening to Music. Finally, Some Good News.

blocks.text: Now this is a very beautiful sūtra.
blocks.directed: Now this is a very beautiful sūtra.

blocks.text: And it deliberately returns us to an earlier teaching.
blocks.directed: And it deliberately returns us to an earlier teaching.

blocks.text: The fourth should be poured into the three like oil.
blocks.directed: The fourth should be poured into the three like oil.

blocks.text: The enlivening of the three by their source.
blocks.directed: The enlivening of the three by their source.

blocks.text: But Kṣemarāja makes an important distinction.
blocks.directed: But Kṣemarāja makes an important distinction.

blocks.text: At 3.20, the discussion centred on the pervasion of waking, dreaming and deep sleep by turya.
blocks.directed: At 3.20, the discussion centred on the pervasion of waking, dreaming and deep sleep by turya.

blocks.text: Here he interprets the three through the dynamics of:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Here he interprets the three through the dynamics of:

blocks.text: And the primary condition underlying all three is:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And the primary condition underlying all three is:

blocks.text: The instruction concerns the infusion of the three conditions with the awareness of their supreme source.
blocks.directed: The instruction concerns the infusion of the three conditions with the awareness of their supreme source.

blocks.text: Now, here’s the truly fascinating part.
blocks.directed: Now, here’s the truly fascinating part.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja associates the three with distinct orientations of experience.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja associates the three with distinct orientations of experience.

blocks.text: Consider what happens when you encounter something beautiful.
blocks.directed: Consider what happens when you encounter something beautiful.

blocks.text: A piece of music, for example.
blocks.directed: A piece of music, for example.

blocks.text: Perhaps the melody becomes extraordinarily moving.
blocks.directed: Perhaps the melody becomes extraordinarily moving.

blocks.text: These three movements can become occasions for recognising the fourth.
blocks.directed: These three movements can become occasions for recognising the fourth.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja says that even when this reality is concealed by Māyā, it can flash forth for an instant.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja says that even when this reality is concealed by Māyā, it can flash forth for an instant.

blocks.text: Now this is a gorgeous image.
blocks.directed: Now this is a gorgeous image.

blocks.text: Because sometimes an experience produces a sudden opening.
blocks.directed: Because sometimes an experience produces a sudden opening.

blocks.text: And for an instant, the ordinary structures of mental limitation can seem to relax.
blocks.directed: And for an instant, the ordinary structures of mental limitation can seem to relax.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja says the practitioner can use such moments to enliven their recognition of the supreme state.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja says the practitioner can use such moments to enliven their recognition of the supreme state.

blocks.text: But the aim is not merely to chase increasingly intense pleasures.
blocks.directed: But the aim is not merely to chase increasingly intense pleasures.

blocks.text: That would simply return us to rāga.
blocks.directed: That would simply return us to rāga.

blocks.text: Searching for completeness in another object.
blocks.directed: Searching for completeness in another object.

blocks.text: Rather, the yogi attends to the underlying conscious reality disclosed through the experience.
blocks.directed: Rather, the yogi attends to the underlying conscious reality disclosed through the experience.

blocks.text: And now Kṣemarāja cites the Vijñānabhairava.
blocks.directed: And now Kṣemarāja cites the Vijñānabhairava.

blocks.text: This is particularly important because the examples are surprisingly diverse.
blocks.directed: This is particularly important because the examples are surprisingly diverse.

blocks.text: He invokes practices involving intense delight, the joy of meeting a beloved person after a long separation, the pleasure of eating and drinking, the experience of music, and even the heightened states associated with sexual enjoyment.
blocks.directed: He invokes practices involving intense delight, the joy of meeting a beloved person after a long separation, the pleasure of eating and drinking, the experience of music, and even the heightened states associated with sexual enjoyment.

blocks.text: The traditional text really does include sensual and erotic examples.
blocks.directed: The traditional text really does include sensual and erotic examples.

blocks.text: We’re not going to pretend it exclusively concerns sitting quietly with a nice cup of herbal tea.
blocks.directed: We’re not going to pretend it exclusively concerns sitting quietly with a nice cup of herbal tea.

blocks.text: But the philosophical point isn’t simply indulgence.
blocks.directed: But the philosophical point isn’t simply indulgence.

blocks.text: It’s the recognition of the conscious fullness that can become apparent through powerful experiences.
blocks.directed: It’s the recognition of the conscious fullness that can become apparent through powerful experiences.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja also invokes the Spandakārikā on intense states such as anger, joy, uncertainty and rapid movement.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja also invokes the Spandakārikā on intense states such as anger, joy, uncertainty and rapid movement.

blocks.text: The common principle is that an unusual intensity of experience may disclose a deeper conscious power when approached through the appropriate contemplative understanding. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: The common principle is that an unusual intensity of experience may disclose a deeper conscious power when approached through the appropriate contemplative understanding. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: This is not a claim that every intense emotion automatically reveals enlightenment.
blocks.directed: This is not a claim that every intense emotion automatically reveals enlightenment.

blocks.text: Nor that sexual pleasure, anger or excitement are inherently liberating.
blocks.directed: Nor that sexual pleasure, anger or excitement are inherently liberating.

blocks.text: The relevant point is the conscious standpoint of the practitioner and the possibility of recognising the source of experience.
blocks.directed: The relevant point is the conscious standpoint of the practitioner and the possibility of recognising the source of experience.

blocks.text: Imagine listening to a piece of music that moves you profoundly.
blocks.directed: Imagine listening to a piece of music that moves you profoundly.

blocks.text: For a moment, the usual sense of being a separate subject evaluating an external object may become less prominent.
blocks.directed: For a moment, the usual sense of being a separate subject evaluating an external object may become less prominent.

blocks.text: Now, you can chase that fullness as something produced exclusively by the external music.
blocks.directed: Now, you can chase that fullness as something produced exclusively by the external music.

blocks.text: Or you can investigate the conscious reality through which the fullness is experienced.
blocks.directed: Or you can investigate the conscious reality through which the fullness is experienced.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja’s argument points towards the latter.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja’s argument points towards the latter.

blocks.text: The delight becomes an occasion for recognising the source.
blocks.directed: The delight becomes an occasion for recognising the source.

blocks.text: But it must not remain merely an isolated flash.
blocks.directed: But it must not remain merely an isolated flash.

blocks.text: The practitioner is instructed to cultivate the continuity of recognition.
blocks.directed: The practitioner is instructed to cultivate the continuity of recognition.

blocks.text: To enliven the successive phases of experience with the conscious reality of turya.
blocks.directed: To enliven the successive phases of experience with the conscious reality of turya.

blocks.text: This is why the word anuprāṇana is so beautiful.
blocks.directed: This is why the word anuprāṇana is so beautiful.

blocks.text: The ordinary processes of manifestation, maintenance and withdrawal become pervaded by recognition.
blocks.directed: The ordinary processes of manifestation, maintenance and withdrawal become pervaded by recognition.

blocks.text: And now we reach the next sūtra.
blocks.directed: And now we reach the next sūtra.

blocks.text: Which extends the method even further.
blocks.directed: Which extends the method even further.

blocks.text: Not merely to particular mental states.
blocks.directed: Not merely to particular mental states.

blocks.text: Not merely to extraordinary moments of joy.
blocks.directed: Not merely to extraordinary moments of joy.

blocks.text: Because apparently no part of experience is permitted to remain outside this recognition.
blocks.directed: Because apparently no part of experience is permitted to remain outside this recognition.

blocks.text: The entire universe is getting spiritually saturated.
blocks.directed: The entire universe is getting spiritually saturated.
